**5B.9 Research Note: Shocks, Inflation, Crises**
**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative on outcomes, but with real evidence of technocratic reform and partial honesty about the severity of the problem.

**Accepted claims**
- **IMF Executive Board Concludes Post Financing Assessment with Nigeria** | IMF | 2024-02-09 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa  
  IMF said Tinubu moved ahead with subsidy removal and FX unification, created a fiscal/tax reform committee, and paired austerity with cereals, subsidized fertilizer, wage awards, and diesel VAT suspension to soften the shock. This is strong evidence of competent shock management with some correction, not just slogans.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.7`

- **Tinubu Establishes Comprehensive Economic Coordination and Planning System for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/  
  Tinubu created PECC/EET structures centered on the finance minister and CBN governor, with economists and private-sector figures, and ordered rapid implementation of an emergency economic plan. That is direct evidence of technocratic crisis coordination.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`

- **World Bank: Turning the Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms  
  The Bank said reforms improved FX supply and narrowed the official/parallel rate gap, while also stressing that inflation and living-cost pain remained severe. This is evidence of some macro competence, but also of incomplete crisis control.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **World Bank: Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification  
  The Bank approved $2.25 billion for stabilization, revenue reforms, and support for the poor. External validation does not prove success, but it does support the view that the reform program was not mere posturing.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Tinubu’s Nationwide Broadcast on the August Protests** | State House | 2024-08-04 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/  
  Tinubu publicly acknowledged deaths, destruction, unrest, and legitimate public frustration tied to bad governance and economic hardship. This is one of the clearest signs of honesty about crisis conditions, though not of successful resolution.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`

- **Tinubu Asks Protesters to Suspend Demonstrations, Seeks Dialogue** | TheCable | 2024-08-04 | https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-tinubu-asks-protesters-to-suspend-demonstrations-seeks-dialogue/  
  Tinubu asked protesters to pause demonstrations to create room for dialogue and said he had heard them “loud and clear.” That is direct evidence of a restraint-oriented crisis response rather than pure denial.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.7`

- **Tinubu Calls for Suspension of Sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso** | State House | 2024-02-24 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/  
  Tinubu urged ECOWAS to choose “a better path” through negotiation and improved governance. This is relevant as a de-escalatory response to a regional shock rather than a prestige-driven escalation.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.7`

- **Tinubu Orders Reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/  
  Procurement reform is a concrete competence signal because it targets a core bottleneck in public spending and crisis response. It also improves transparency when the state is under pressure.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`

- **Tinubu Directs Prioritization of Digital Infrastructure Investment** | State House | 2024-03-14 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-prioritization-of-digital-infrastructure-investment-to-enhance-business-efficiency-and-productivity/  
  Tinubu ordered ministries to align regulations and tax frameworks to speed broadband and telecom investment, showing a specific corrective move in a productivity-sensitive sector.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.6`, `5B.7`

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Nigeria: Hundreds Gather Across Nigerian Cities to Protest Cost-of-Living Crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376  
  Reuters tied protests to subsidy removal, naira devaluation, electricity tariffs, and inflation above 34 percent, showing that the shock response had not yet stabilized living conditions. This is strong negative evidence for competence in outcomes.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.8`

- **Nigeria: Insecurity, Rising Costs Push 31 Million Nigerians into Acute Food Shortage** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474  
  The acute food shortage scale is strong negative evidence that the reform path had not yet protected the most vulnerable from inflation and shocks.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.8`

- **Nigeria: Staying the Course on Reforms, Progress Amidst Challenges** | World Bank | 2024-10-17 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/nigeria-staying-the-course-on-reforms-progress-amidst-challenges  
  The Bank said macro stability, fiscal health, and reserves improved, but inflation stayed high and households and businesses still faced short-term pain. This is mixed, but the remaining pain is important negative evidence against full competence.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **FG Spent N63.6bn on Military Equipment in Seven Months - Report** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/  
  Weakly disclosed security spending raises diversion and opportunity-cost concerns, especially during a period of household distress. Even if security-driven, it weakens the case for disciplined shock management.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.3`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`

- **Nigeria Considers Tough Penalties for ‘Subversive’ Acts Under Proposed Law** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-14 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782  
  A proposed counter-subversion bill was criticized as a crackdown on dissent. Even though later withdrawn, it suggests a tendency toward scapegoating and coercive crisis politics rather than transparent learning.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`

- **Nigeria Charges Protesters With Treason and Mutiny After August Demonstrations** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02 | https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/  
  Prosecutors framed protesters as destabilizers and mutineers. That is negative evidence for honest crisis handling because it recasts a cost-of-living protest as a security threat rather than addressing the underlying economic shock.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`

- **Amnesty Says Police Used Excessive Force to Violently Quash Endbadgovernance Protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/  
  Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the crackdown. That is strong evidence that crisis management was not consistently competent or rights-respecting in practice.  
  IDs: `5B.9`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on inflation, subsidy shock, protests, FX stabilization, and crisis rhetoric.
- I did not find equally strong direct evidence on unemployment-specific policy performance or debt-management outcomes in 2024 in the sources I used.
- So the best-supported reading is: Tinubu’s team showed real technocratic intent and some honest acknowledgment of the crisis, but the year still ended with severe inflation, food stress, protest repression, and incomplete stabilization.
